entries.clue: Satisfied, virtually cancel mass chemical processes (10)

indicatorNotes.virtually: virtually all of a word: its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: ABOLISH = cancel, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone content to scrap large-scale chemical work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Satisfied' looks like an adjective describing the person, but it is the verb MET, as in a demand met.
annotation.definitionFit: Metabolism is the set of chemical processes that keep a living body going.

entries.clue: One way to control rioting staff (4)

blocks.note: a chemical spray police use to subdue a crowd
an ornamental rod carried before a mayor or in Parliament

annotation.surface: Riot police choosing how to keep order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staff' tempts as police personnel, fitting the riot picture; it is the ceremonial rod.
annotation.definitionFit: Mace is a spray that disables rioters, and a mace is also an ornamental staff carried in ceremony.

entries.clue: So briefly, there’s nothing in that for you (4)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short: the last letter goes

annotation.surface: A curt warning that there is no gain in something for you.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'there's nothing in that' literally: O sits inside THU, the shortened 'so'. 'Thou' is the old form of 'you'.
annotation.definitionFit: Thou is the archaic singular form of you.

entries.clue: Not hard for stroke on river, the way the oar moves (4,3,5)

indicatorNotes.Not: not hard: the H (hard) is taken out

blocks.note: BACKHAND is a stroke in tennis; drop H = hard
the Forth is a Scottish river; 'on' puts it next

annotation.surface: A rowing coach telling a stroke to ease off on the river.
annotation.walkthrough: In a rowing surface 'stroke' means the rower setting the pace, but here it is a tennis stroke, the backhand. H = hard, as on pencils.
annotation.definitionFit: An oar travels back and forth, to and fro, with each stroke.

entries.clue: Grub is hot stuff, with a pinch of rosemary in (5)

indicatorNotes.a pinch of: a pinch is a tiny amount: just the first letter
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the herb's letter inside the lava, as a pinch of herb goes into a dish

blocks.note: its first letter, placed inside LAVA

annotation.surface: A cook describing a spicy dish seasoned with a little rosemary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grub' reads as food, fitting the cooking scene; it is the insect larva.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: grub is the everyday word for the soft young stage of a beetle or similar insect.

entries.clue: Sorry to engage a pupil to deliver cold meal here (5,4)

blocks.note: A + L, a learner, placed inside SAD
in cricket, to bowl is to deliver the ball

annotation.surface: An apology for hiring a student to bring round cold food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' reads as a food delivery; in cricket the bowler delivers the ball. L = learner, from the L-plates on a learner's car.
annotation.definitionFit: A salad bowl is the dish where a cold meal of salad is served.

entries.clue: Poet Robert missing half the summit (4)

indicatorNotes.missing half: half the name is taken away

blocks.note: BROWNING without its second half, NING

annotation.surface: A remark that the poet Robert has not quite reached the top.
annotation.walkthrough: Robert Browning is the Victorian poet; eight letters, so half leaves BROW.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in landscape terms: the brow of a hill is its crest.

entries.clue: Violent partners rule over trembling daughter (5,5)

indicatorNotes.trembling: shaking the letters into a new order

annotation.surface: A domestic scene of abusive partners and a frightened daughter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rule over' looks like a single verb, dominate; it is two abbreviations, R and O. Rough trade is slang for casual, often violent, sexual partners.
annotation.definitionFit: Rough trade is slang for sexual partners who are rough or violent.

entries.clue: All those that somehow managed to upset priest (10)

indicatorNotes.managed: the letters are handled into a new order
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, turned upside down

blocks.note: Rev = Reverend, turned over to VER

annotation.surface: Everyone who contrived to offend the priest.
annotation.walkthrough: The adverb in the surface is not part of the story but the seven letters of fodder; Rev is the abbreviation for a clergyman.
annotation.definitionFit: Whomsoever means any or all persons that, in an object role.

entries.clue: Cut round field pattern (4,6)

annotation.surface: Instructions to mow around a field in a pattern.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut round' reads as one instruction, to trim around; it splits into two nouns.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: the designs flattened into cornfields, often blamed on aliens.

entries.clue: Are you aware of speaking badly of goddess? (4)

indicatorNotes.speaking badly: slurred speech runs the words together into a sound

annotation.surface: Someone asking if you realise you're insulting a goddess.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Speaking badly of' looks like slander, but it describes careless pronunciation: 'd'you know' slurs to 'Juno'.
annotation.definitionFit: Juno is the Roman queen of the gods.

entries.clue: Playing without knowing the score? (5-7)

blocks.note: the surface suggests a game; the setter means performing music
the surface suggests an unknown match result; the setter means written music never seen before

annotation.surface: A sports player unaware of the scoreline.
annotation.walkthrough: The score is not the match tally but the written music: a sight-reader plays a piece without having learnt it.
annotation.definitionFit: Sight-reading is playing written music at first sight, without prior knowledge of the score.

entries.clue: Take a chance on answers here: two blinking indicators (6,6)

blocks.note: to hazard = to risk, as in hazard a guess
in crosswords, the answers entered in the grid are called lights

annotation.surface: A solver about to guess, with a nod to two flashing signals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Answers here' points at the grid itself: crossword answers are known as lights.
annotation.definitionFit: Hazard lights are a car's paired indicators blinking together as a warning.

entries.clue: As chemist I must twice intervene in equine therapy (5,5)

indicatorNotes.intervene in: to intervene is to come between: I goes inside

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse

annotation.surface: A chemist insisting on stepping in, twice, to treat a horse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Twice' is the key: one I intervenes in each word, so the horse and the therapy each gain a letter. 'Equine' is an adjective standing for a horse.
annotation.definitionFit: Marie Curie was the Nobel-winning chemist who discovered radium.

entries.clue: Some friend you are, I would say, sort of sloppy (10)

indicatorNotes.I would say: spoken aloud, 'you are' becomes the letters U R

blocks.note: the letters U and R sound like 'you are', as in text-speak

annotation.surface: An exasperated 'some friend you are', calling someone careless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some friend you are' reads as a sarcastic put-down; the 'you are' part is text-speak, where letters stand in for their sounds.
annotation.definitionFit: Amateurish work is sloppy, lacking professional skill.

entries.clue: On branch, notice sick old animal (9)

blocks.note: an arm = a branch of an organisation

annotation.surface: Someone spotting an ailing old animal up on a branch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Branch' and 'notice' look like a tree and seeing; they are ARM and AD.
annotation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured American mammal.

entries.clue: Rewarding to be touring capitals, rapidly attracting trade from the beginning (9)

indicatorNotes.touring: going round: LIVE surrounds the rest
indicatorNotes.from the beginning: take the start of each word

annotation.surface: A travel business finding it pays to tour capital cities and pull in trade fast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capitals' suggests cities; it is UC, printers' shorthand for upper-case letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a lucrative job or deal is one that pays well, rewarding in money.

entries.clue: Heard husky in bay perhaps (5)

indicatorNotes.Heard: the word as it sounds, not as it is spelt

annotation.surface: A husky dog's voice picked up in a bay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Husky' reads as a sled dog and 'bay' as barking; husky is hoarse, and a bay is a reddish-brown horse.
annotation.definitionFit: A bay is a horse with a reddish-brown coat, so a horse by example.

entries.clue: Opening passage, repaint Roman walls (5)

indicatorNotes.walls: the words enclose the answer, as walls do

annotation.surface: Instructions to repaint the Roman walls at the entrance passage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Walls' looks like the thing being painted; it is the verb, the two words walling in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A shortening: intro is informal for introduction, the opening section of a song or piece.

entries.clue: El Greco I’d mistaken for a poet (9)

indicatorNotes.mistaken: the letters are got wrong, rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone confusing the painter El Greco with a poet.
annotation.walkthrough: A painter mistaken for a poet is the picture, and the painter's name really does rearrange into one.
annotation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor Coleridge was an English Romantic poet.

entries.clue: Proceeding in field to woo maiden, not complete? No pressure! (5,7)

indicatorNotes.No: no pressure: the P is removed

blocks.note: M = maiden, a scoreless over in cricket
PARTIAL = not complete, without P = pressure

annotation.surface: A suitor wooing a girl gently, with no pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Field' is the battlefield: a court martial is a military trial, held in the field.
annotation.definitionFit: A court martial is a legal proceeding held by the armed forces, including in the field.

entries.clue: Regularly burn out defective power source in car (5)

indicatorNotes.Regularly: 'Regularly' means at regular intervals, so only every other letter of the word is kept
indicatorNotes.defective: faulty, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: B and R, every other letter of BURN

annotation.surface: A warning that a faulty car engine part keeps burning out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Burn out' reads as one phrasal verb; only 'burn' is thinned, and 'out' joins it whole.
annotation.definitionFit: A turbo is a turbocharger, which boosts a car engine's power.

entries.clue: Riddle to floor a number (4)

annotation.surface: A puzzle that stumps plenty of people.
annotation.walkthrough: A koan is a paradoxical riddle used in Zen Buddhism.
annotation.definitionFit: A koan is a Zen riddle with no logical answer, set for meditation.

entries.clue: Doctrines compressed into one text (4)

annotation.surface: Whole belief systems squeezed into a single piece of writing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Text' suggests a book; it is an SMS on a phone, and a text message is, fittingly, compressed.
annotation.definitionFit: Isms are doctrines or ideologies, named for the suffix.

entries.clue: Bucket needing great physical effort? No way (4)

blocks.note: STRAIN without ST = street, a way

annotation.surface: Lifting a heavy bucket is too much effort: no way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bucket' is a verb: when it buckets, it rains heavily. ST (street) is a standard 'way'.
annotation.definitionFit: To bucket down is to rain very hard.

entries.clue: Creature of the harvest endlessly eating one crop, such a headache (10)

annotation.definitionNote: adjective: of the kind of headache called migraine

indicatorNotes.eating: the creature takes the rest inside

blocks.note: a harvest mouse; MOUSE without its end

annotation.surface: A harvest mouse gorging on the crop, and what a headache it is.
annotation.walkthrough: The harvest mouse is a real species, so 'creature of the harvest' is MOUSE. Migrainous is a rare but genuine medical word.
annotation.definitionFit: Migrainous describes a headache of migraine type.

entries.clue: Another chance to hear letter on the radio (4)

blocks.note: a sound bounced back off a wall or cliff
the radio code word for E in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A radio broadcast repeated so a letter can be heard again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the radio' tempts as a broadcast repeat; it means the radio alphabet, where E is Echo.
annotation.definitionFit: An echo lets you hear a sound a second time, and Echo is radio code for E.

entries.clue: Show keenness to break into people’s stuff (10)

indicatorNotes.to break into: one part forces its way inside the other

blocks.note: to long = to yearn, show keenness

annotation.surface: A burglar eager to break into someone's house for their stuff.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture is a burglary, but 'break into' is the container signal; reading the possessive as 'people has' is a common crossword liberty.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stuff in the casual sense of possessions, the things that belong to you.
